#### Closed sets are string unions, not numbers or IntEnums

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `ErrorCode` | ErrorCode is a const object plus same-named union type instead of a TS enum; there is no reverse mapping, and StaleResult = 11 is added |
| `Mode` (`./analysis`) | removed: Use KeyMode: the strings 'major', 'minor', 'dorian', 'phrygian', 'lydian', 'mixolydian', 'locrian'; the numeric Mode constants are gone. |
| `Mode` | removed: Use KeyMode: the strings 'major', 'minor', 'dorian', 'phrygian', 'lydian', 'mixolydian', 'locrian'; the numeric Mode constants are gone. |

#### Two-dimensional results are one Matrix2D type

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `Matrix2dResult` | `Matrix2D` |

#### Public types never expose Wasm* names

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `FrameResult` | removed: frameSignal returns a Matrix2D (samples on rows, frames on columns); read its rows, cols and data |
| `SonareModule` | removed: an Emscripten module type, no longer exported; the moduleFactory option of init() takes a ModuleFactory, which resolves the opaque ModuleHandle and is the default export of @libraz/libsonare/module |

#### Cancellation uses signal for promises and cancel for sync calls

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `OfflineWorkerClient.analyze(options)` | pass { signal } to cancel; the call returns a Promise instead of OfflineWorkerTask; onProgress moves to the request as (progress, stage) |
| `OfflineWorkerClient.detectBpm` | returns Promise; cancel with options.signal; request takes onProgress |
| `OfflineWorkerClient.detectChords` | returns Promise; cancel with options.signal; request takes onProgress |
| `OfflineWorkerClient.detectKey` | returns Promise; cancel with options.signal; request takes onProgress |
| `OfflineWorkerClient.masterAudioStereo` | returns Promise; cancel with options.signal; request takes onProgress |
| `OfflineWorkerClient.masterAudio` | returns Promise; cancel with options.signal; request takes onProgress; a cancel field is refused |
| `OfflineWorkerTask` | removed: Await the promise OfflineWorkerClient methods return; pass { signal } with an AbortController to cancel, which rejects with a SonareError coded Cancelled. |

#### Progress is an onProgress option, not a separate function

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `Audio.analyzeWithProgress` | removed: call analyze with onProgress in the options |
| `OfflineWorkerCallOptions.onProgress` | removed: pass onProgress in the request object; it receives (progress, stage) on the calling thread |
| `OfflineWorkerProgress` | removed: removed with the options callback; the request onProgress takes (progress, stage) as ProgressCallback |

#### Onset strength has one name on every surface

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `Audio.onsetEnvelope` | `Audio.onsetStrength` |

| `Audio.detectBpm` | searches 60-200 BPM by default (was 30-300); bpmMin/bpmMax narrow it |
| `Audio.detectDownbeats` | the beat grid under it searches 60-200 BPM (was 30-300) |

#### Errors are coded by cause on every surface

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `Audio.fromMemoryWithBrowserFallback` | fallback failures throw SonareError NotSupported (no decoding context) or DecodeFailed with the decoder error as cause |
| `ErrorCode.AbiMismatch` | a C-ABI failure coded as an ABI mismatch (10) now arrives as SonareError AbiMismatch instead of InvalidState |
| `ErrorCode.Unknown` | a C-ABI failure the library codes as unknown (99) now arrives as SonareError Unknown instead of InvalidState |
| `OfflineWorkerClient` | constructor without a Worker throws SonareError NotSupported; a worker crash or malformed message rejects pending calls with a SonareError |
| `SonareError.codeName` | typed as the ErrorCodeName union instead of string, and derived from code |
| `SonareError.code` | typed as the ErrorCode union instead of number |

#### Cheap scalar state reads are getters and properties

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `Audio.data` | data is one shared Float32Array read on every access; do not mutate it, copy with slice() first |

#### Each operation has exactly one entry point

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `Audio.masteringChain` | removed: Call masterAudio({ preset, overrides }); the old config is now overrides. |
| `Audio.stftDb` | removed: Call audio.stft({ db: true }); the result then also carries db. |

#### masterAudio is the mastering entry; mastering is renamed

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `Audio.masteringProcess` | `Audio.masteringApplyProcessor`: renamed to masteringApplyProcessor<P extends SoloProcessor>(options: OptionsOf<MasteringApplyProcessorRequest<P>>): MasteringResult |
| `Audio.mastering` | `Audio.masteringNormalizeLoudness`: renamed to masteringNormalizeLoudness(options?: MasteringNormalizeLoudnessOptions): MasteringNormalizeLoudnessResult |

#### Synchronous construction is new X(config); create() is async

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `Audio` | new Audio(...) is a TypeError naming the factories: build one with Audio.fromBuffer or another factory |

#### Setters take labelled objects, not positional booleans

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `Audio.masterAudio(onProgress)` | removed: pass onProgress as a field of MasterAudioRequest |
| `Audio.masterAudio(overrides)` | removed: pass overrides as a field of MasterAudioRequest |
| `Audio.masterAudio(presetName)` | removed: pass it as preset in MasterAudioRequest |
| `Audio.masterAudio` | masterAudio(options: OptionsOf<MasterAudioRequest>): MasteringChainResult; options must give preset or overrides |
| `Audio.melSpectrogram(htk)` | removed: pass htk as a field of MelSpectrogramRequest |
| `Audio.mfcc(htk)` | removed: pass htk as a field of MfccRequest |
| `Audio.pitchPyin(fillNa)` | removed: pass fillNa as a field of PitchPyinRequest |
| `Audio.pitchYin(fillNa)` | removed: had no effect: YIN reads no fill flag, so PitchYinRequest has no fillNa (pitchPyin keeps it) |

#### Pitch and formant shifts are named in semitones

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `Audio.pitchShift(semitones)` | removed: pass it as pitchSemitones in PitchShiftRequest |
| `Audio.pitchShift` | pitchShift(options: Omit<PitchShiftRequest,'samples'\|'sampleRate'>) |

#### One type name per record on every surface

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `EqBand` | `EqBandInput` |
| `SonareCapabilities` (`./analysis`) | `Capabilities` |
| `SonareCapabilities` | `Capabilities` |
| `SonareScopeRingBuffer` (`./worklet`) | `ScopeRingBuffer` |
| `SonareScopeRingReadResult` (`./worklet`) | `ScopeRingReadResult` |
| `readSonareScopeRingBuffer` (`./worklet`) | `readScopeRingBuffer` |

#### Historical aliases are removed

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `CapabilityCatalogChain.aliases` (`./analysis`) | removed: the catalog lists no other chain spellings; every chain key has exactly one |
| `CapabilityCatalogChain.aliases` | removed: the catalog lists no other chain spellings; every chain key has exactly one |
| `CapabilityCatalogChainAlias` (`./analysis`) | removed: the catalog lists no other chain spellings; every chain key has exactly one |
| `CapabilityCatalogChainAlias` | removed: the catalog lists no other chain spellings; every chain key has exactly one |
| `EqBand.lookaheadMs` (`./analysis`) | removed: use detectorDelayMs |
| `EqBand.lookaheadMs` | removed: use detectorDelayMs |
| `hasFfmpegSupport` (`./analysis`) | removed: read capabilities().features.ffmpeg |
| `hasFfmpegSupport` | removed: read capabilities().features.ffmpeg |
| `vocalEditAvailable` | removed: read capabilities().features.vocalEdit |

#### Versions and features come from *AbiVersion() and capabilities()

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `EXPECTED_ABI_VERSION` (`./analysis`) | removed: no longer exported; the binding checks ABI compatibility at load and throws AbiMismatch, and capabilities().abi reports the loaded versions |
| `EXPECTED_ABI_VERSION` (`./worklet`) | removed: no longer exported; the binding checks ABI compatibility at load and throws AbiMismatch, and capabilities().abi reports the loaded versions |
| `EXPECTED_ABI_VERSION` | removed: no longer exported; the binding checks ABI compatibility at load and throws AbiMismatch, and capabilities().abi reports the loaded versions |
| `EXPECTED_ENGINE_ABI_VERSION` | removed: no longer exported; the binding checks ABI compatibility at load and throws AbiMismatch, and capabilities().abi reports the loaded versions |

#### Other individual changes

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `Audio.detectClipping` | delegates to meteringDetectClipping: an unknown option key is a TypeError reading 'Audio.detectClipping: unknown key k (expected ...)' (was "unknown option 'k'") |
| `Audio.dynamicRange` | delegates to meteringDynamicRange: an unknown option key is a TypeError reading 'Audio.dynamicRange: unknown key k (expected ...)' (was "unknown option 'k'") |
| `Audio.spectrumFrame` | delegates to meteringSpectrumFrame: an unknown option key is a TypeError reading 'Audio.spectrumFrame: unknown key k (expected ...)' (was "unknown option 'k'"); an explicit nFft of 0 is a RangeError |
| `Audio.spectrum` | delegates to meteringSpectrum: an unknown option key is a TypeError reading 'Audio.spectrum: unknown key k (expected ...)' (was "unknown option 'k'"); an explicit nFft of 0 is a RangeError |
| `createSonareScopeRingBuffer` (`./worklet`) | `createScopeRingBuffer`: takes one options object { capacity, bands, maxPoints } instead of positional numbers; an unknown key is a TypeError, a non-integer or out-of-domain value a RangeError |
| `sonareScopeRingBufferByteLength` (`./worklet`) | `scopeRingBufferByteLength`: takes one options object { capacity, bands, maxPoints } instead of positional numbers; an unknown key is a TypeError, a non-integer or out-of-domain value a RangeError |

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|

| `RealtimeVoiceChanger.processPreparedMono` | removed: Use createRealtimeMonoBuffer(numSamples): fill its input view and call its process(). |
| `RealtimeVoiceChanger.processPreparedPlanar` | removed: Use createRealtimePlanarBuffer(numFrames, numChannels): fill its channels and call its process(). |
| `RealtimeVoiceChanger.setPodConfig` | removed: Call setConfig(config), which takes the same config object. |
| `decomposeWithInit` (`./analysis`) | removed: Call decompose({ s, nComponents, init: 'nndsvd' }); init is a field of DecomposeRequest. |
| `decomposeWithInit` | removed: Call decompose({ s, nComponents, init: 'nndsvd' }); init is a field of DecomposeRequest. |

| `hpssWithResidual` | removed: Call hpss({ samples, sampleRate, withResidual: true }); the result then also carries residual. |

| `masteringChain` | removed: Call masterAudio({ samples, sampleRate, preset, overrides }); the old config is now overrides, and sampleRate is required. |

| `meteringPhaseScopeDecimated` | removed: Call meteringPhaseScope({ left, right, sampleRate, maxPoints }); maxPoints is a field of MeteringPhaseScopeRequest. |

| `MasteringChainConfig` | sent to the core as a version 2 chain document: a dotted key names the same path as its nesting, and the core refuses an unknown or retired key, a wrong-kind leaf, a number on a token path, an unknown token or one path given twice, naming the path under the request key it came in (overrides, config): TypeError for a wrong shape, RangeError for an out-of-domain value or unknown token, as from the 1.x facade; a non-object config stays a TypeError; null, which is also what a NaN or an infinity serializes to, is a TypeError, and an empty list a RangeError |

### WASM: Realtime engine, synthesis, MIDI and playback

#### Sample rate is required wherever samples are passed

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `PlaybackRendererOptions.sampleRate` | required (was optional with a 48000 default) |

#### Handles are released with destroy() and close()

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `BindMicrophoneInputOptions.stopTracksOnClose` | `BindMicrophoneInputOptions.stopTracksOnDestroy` |
| `HrtfSet.delete` | removed: call destroy() |
| `MicrophoneInputBinding.close` | `MicrophoneInputBinding.destroy` |
| `Mixer.delete` | removed: call destroy() |
| `PlaybackLoudnessMeter.delete` | removed: call destroy() |
| `PlaybackRenderer.delete` | removed: call destroy() |
| `RealtimeEngine.delete` | removed: call destroy() |
| `SampleBank.delete` | removed: call destroy() |
| `WebMidiBinding.close` | `WebMidiBinding.destroy` |

#### Classes that wait on a worker destroy asynchronously

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `SonareRealtimeEngineNode.destroy` (`./worklet`) | destroy() returns Promise<void>; await it or use await using |

#### Seconds are spelled Sec and _sec

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `EngineCapturePunchRequest` | `CapturePunch`: renamed CapturePunch with startPpq/endPpq added; the enabled flag is gone, a punch window is active while CaptureOptions.punch is given |
| `EngineMetronomeConfig.clickSeconds` | `EngineMetronomeConfig.clickSec` |
| `SonareEngineTransportFacade.seekSeconds(seconds)` (`./worklet`) | `SonareEngineTransportFacade.seekSec(timeSec)`: a negative, NaN or infinite position is refused with RangeError instead of being posted to the worklet |

#### Physical quantities carry their unit in the name

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `SonareEngineTransportFacade.play(sampleTime)` (`./worklet`) | `SonareEngineTransportFacade.play(renderFrame)` |
| `SonareEngineTransportFacade.seekPpq(sampleTime)` (`./worklet`) | `SonareEngineTransportFacade.seekPpq(renderFrame)` |
| `SonareEngineTransportFacade.seekSeconds(sampleTime)` (`./worklet`) | `SonareEngineTransportFacade.seekSec(renderFrame)` |
| `SonareEngineTransportFacade.stop(sampleTime)` (`./worklet`) | `SonareEngineTransportFacade.stop(renderFrame)` |
| `SonareRealtimeEngineNode.play(sampleTime)` (`./worklet`) | `SonareRealtimeEngineNode.play(renderFrame)` |
| `SonareRealtimeEngineNode.resetMasterLoudnessMeter(sampleTime)` (`./worklet`) | `SonareRealtimeEngineNode.resetMasterLoudnessMeter(renderFrame)` |
| `SonareRealtimeEngineNode.resetProcessorState(sampleTime)` (`./worklet`) | `SonareRealtimeEngineNode.resetProcessorState(renderFrame)` |
| `SonareRealtimeEngineNode.seekPpq(sampleTime)` (`./worklet`) | `SonareRealtimeEngineNode.seekPpq(renderFrame)` |
| `SonareRealtimeEngineNode.seekSample(sampleTime)` (`./worklet`) | `SonareRealtimeEngineNode.seekSample(renderFrame)` |
| `SonareRealtimeEngineNode.stop(sampleTime)` (`./worklet`) | `SonareRealtimeEngineNode.stop(renderFrame)` |
| `WebMidiEngine.pushMidiInputCc(time)` | `WebMidiEngine.pushMidiInputCc(offsetInBlockSamples)` |
| `WebMidiEngine.pushMidiInputChannelPressure(time)` | `WebMidiEngine.pushMidiInputChannelPressure(offsetInBlockSamples)` |
| `WebMidiEngine.pushMidiInputNoteOff(time)` | `WebMidiEngine.pushMidiInputNoteOff(offsetInBlockSamples)` |
| `WebMidiEngine.pushMidiInputNoteOn(time)` | `WebMidiEngine.pushMidiInputNoteOn(offsetInBlockSamples)` |
| `WebMidiEngine.pushMidiInputPitchBend(time)` | `WebMidiEngine.pushMidiInputPitchBend(offsetInBlockSamples)` |
| `WebMidiEngine.pushMidiInputPolyPressure(time)` | `WebMidiEngine.pushMidiInputPolyPressure(offsetInBlockSamples)` |
| `WebMidiEngine.pushMidiInputUmp(time)` | `WebMidiEngine.pushMidiInputUmp(offsetInBlockSamples)` |

#### Loudness quantities use one name per measurement

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `EngineMeterTelemetry.maxTruePeakDb` | `EngineMeterTelemetry.maxTruePeakDbtp`: maxTruePeakDb -> maxTruePeakDbtp |
| `EngineMeterTelemetry.truePeakDbL` | `EngineMeterTelemetry.truePeakDbtp`: truePeakDbL -> truePeakDbtp[0]: one entry per plane, numChannels long |
| `EngineMeterTelemetry.truePeakDbR` | `EngineMeterTelemetry.truePeakDbtp`: truePeakDbR -> truePeakDbtp[1]: one entry per plane, numChannels long |

#### A value that is not given is absent, never 0, -1 or ''

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `EngineBounceOptions.blockSize` | the 1.x default value is gone: omit it for the library default; an explicit 0 is a RangeError |
| `EngineBounceOptions.ditherBits` | with dither set, an integer in [2, 32]: 0, 1 and 33 are a RangeError reading 'options.ditherBits must be an integer in [2, 32]' (0 used to select 16) |
| `EngineBounceOptions.ditherSeed` | 0 is the seed 0; omit it for the default seed (1.x read 0 as the default seed) |
| `EngineBounceOptions.numChannels` | required; no channel count is assumed |
| `EngineBounceOptions.sourceSampleRate` | absent means the engine rate; an explicit 0 is a RangeError |
| `EngineBounceOptions.targetSampleRate` | absent keeps the source rate; an explicit 0 is a RangeError |
| `EngineBus.outputBusId` | absent routes to the master mix; an explicit 0 is a RangeError |
| `EngineCapturePunchRequest.enabled` | removed: a punch window is active while CaptureOptions.punch is given; omit punch to record without one |
| `EngineClip.lengthSamples` | omit it to play to the end of the source; an explicit 0 is a RangeError reading 'clips[i].lengthSamples must be an integer of at least 1' (0 used to select the end of the source) |
| `EngineFreezeOptions.blockSize` | the 1.x default value is gone: omit it for the library default; an explicit 0 is a RangeError |
| `EngineFreezeOptions.clipId` | omit it for the default clip id; an explicit 0 is a RangeError reading 'RealtimeEngine.freezeOffline: clipId must not be 0; omit it for the default', any other value an integer in [1, 4294967295] |
| `EngineFreezeOptions.numChannels` | required; no channel count is assumed |
| `EngineMetronomeConfig.clickSamples` | clickSamples and clickSec are both optional: omit both for the click length derived from the click duration; an explicit 0 on either is a RangeError (clickSamples in [1, 384000], clickSec in (0, 1]), and giving both is a RangeError |
| `EngineMidiClipSchedule.lengthSamples` | omit it for an open-ended clip; an explicit 0 is a RangeError reading 'clips[i].lengthSamples must be an integer of at least 1' (0 used to select open-ended) |
| `EngineMidiClipSchedule.loopLengthSamples` | an integer of at least 1, required on a looping clip; an explicit 0 is a RangeError reading 'clips[i].loopLengthSamples must be an integer of at least 1' |
| `EngineTrackLane.outputBusId` | absent routes to the master mix; an explicit 0 is a RangeError |
| `Mixer` | maxBlockSize: the 1.x default value is gone: omit it for the library default; an explicit 0 is a RangeError |
| `PlaybackRendererOptions.maxBlockSize` | the 1.x default value is gone: omit it for the library default; an explicit 0 is a RangeError |
| `RealtimeEngine.metronome` | returns EngineMetronomeConfig carrying only the click-length spelling that was set |
| `RealtimeEngine.popClipPageRequest` | returns undefined (was null) when no request is queued |
| `RealtimeEngine.primeOfflineParameters` | blockSize is optional: omit it for the library default; an explicit 0 is a RangeError |
| `RealtimeEngine.setTrackOutputBus` | setTrackOutputBus(trackId, busId: number \| null): null routes to the master mix and 0 is a RangeError |
| `RenderOfflineRequest.blockSize` | the 1.x default value is gone: omit it for the library default; an explicit 0 is a RangeError |
| `SidechainCheck.reason` | T \| null -> optional: a value the result cannot give is an absent field, never null |
| `SonareEngine.setTrackOutputBus` (`./worklet`) | setTrackOutputBus(target, busId: number \| null): null routes to the master, 0 is a RangeError |

#### A number outside its domain is refused, never passed through

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `EngineBounceOptions.targetLufs` | absent means -14; any finite value, 0 included, is a literal target; a non-finite value is refused |
| `Mixer.processStereoInto` | an input list that is not array-like is refused with TypeError naming leftInputs and rightInputs (it used to read as no inputs and mix nothing), and a non-array input channel is a TypeError naming the element instead of a channel-length RangeError |
| `RealtimeEngine.setTempoSegments` | a missing (undefined or null) or non-array-like segment list is refused with TypeError, so pass [] to clear the map (a missing list used to clear it silently); a non-integer, negative or wrapped length is refused by name, and a list over the input budget with RangeError |
| `RealtimeEngine.setTempo` | a NaN, infinite or out-of-range bpm is refused with RangeError naming it (1.x passed it through) |
| `RealtimeEngine.setTimeSignatureSegments` | a missing (undefined or null) or non-array-like segment list is refused with TypeError, so pass [] to clear the map (a missing list used to clear it silently); a non-integer, negative or wrapped length is refused by name, and a list over the input budget with RangeError |
| `SonareEngine.setTempo` (`./worklet`) | a NaN, infinite or out-of-range bpm is refused with RangeError naming it before anything is posted to the processor (1.x passed it through) |
| `SonareEngineTransportFacade.setTempo` (`./worklet`) | a NaN, infinite or out-of-range bpm is refused with RangeError naming it before anything is posted to the processor (1.x passed it through) |

#### Each list input takes one item form

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |

| `PlaybackRendererOptions.config` | PlaybackRendererConfig object only; a JSON string is a TypeError, and the core refuses an unknown key, a 1.x snake_case key or role token at any depth as SonareError InvalidFormat |
| `RealtimeEngine.pushMidiUmp` | words is a Uint32Array or number array; a bare number is a TypeError |
| `RenderPlaybackRequest.config` | PlaybackRendererConfig object only; a JSON string is a TypeError |

#### RealtimeEngine and SonareEngine share one vocabulary

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `EngineTelemetry.graphLatencySamplesQ8` | `EngineTelemetry.graphLatencySamples` |
| `EngineTransportState.barCount` | `EngineTransportState.barIndex` |
| `RealtimeEngine.graphLatencySamplesQ8` | `RealtimeEngine.graphLatencySamples` |
| `RealtimeEngine.setBuiltinInstrument` | setBuiltinInstrument(destinationId?, config?); absent or null is destination 0; config.destinationId is refused |
| `RealtimeEngine.setCaptureBuffer` | removed: Call configureCapture({ capacityFrames, numChannels? }); it sets the buffer together with source, offset, monitor and punch. |
| `RealtimeEngine.setCapturePunch` | removed: Call configureCapture({ capacityFrames, punch: { startSample, endSample } }); startSec/endSec or startPpq/endPpq work too, and omitting punch clears the window. |
| `RealtimeEngine.setCaptureSource` | removed: Call configureCapture({ capacityFrames, source }) with source 'output' or 'input'; the call states the whole capture setup. |
| `RealtimeEngine.setInputMonitor` | removed: Call configureCapture({ capacityFrames, inputMonitor: { enabled, gain? } }); the call states the whole capture setup. |
| `RealtimeEngine.setMarkers` | an entry's id is optional and an absent one is assigned, as SonareEngine.setMarkers does; returns the stored EngineMarker[] in the order given |
| `RealtimeEngine.setRecordOffsetSamples` | removed: Call configureCapture({ capacityFrames, recordOffsetSamples }); the call states the whole capture setup. |
| `RealtimeEngine.setSf2Instrument` | setSf2Instrument(destinationId?, config?); absent or null is destination 0; config.destinationId is refused |

### WASM: Projects, arrangement and vocal editing

#### Sample rate is required wherever samples are passed

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `ProjectLoopRecordingDesc.audioSampleRate` | required: the rate of the caller's capture has no default (was 48000) |

#### Handles are released with destroy() and close()

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `ClipPageProvider.delete` | removed: call destroy() |
| `ClipPageStreamer.close` | removed: call destroy() |
| `ClipPageStreamer.delete` | removed: call destroy() |
| `OpfsClipPageProviderBinding.close` | `OpfsClipPageProviderBinding.destroy` |
| `Project.delete` | removed: call destroy() |
| `ProjectTimeline.delete` | removed: call destroy() |
| `ProjectTimeline.dispose` | removed: call destroy() |
| `VocalEditDraft.delete` | removed: call destroy() |
| `VocalEditDraft.dispose` | removed: call destroy() |
| `VocalEditSession.delete` | removed: call destroy() |
| `VocalEditSession.dispose` | removed: call destroy() |
| `VocalEditWorkerNativeDraft.dispose` (`./vocal-edit-worker`) | `VocalEditWorkerNativeDraft.destroy` |
| `VocalEditWorkerNativeSession.dispose` (`./vocal-edit-worker`) | `VocalEditWorkerNativeSession.destroy` |
| `VocalRenderJob.delete` | removed: call destroy() |
| `VocalRenderJob.dispose` | removed: call destroy() |
| `VocalRenderSnapshot.delete` | removed: call destroy() |
| `VocalRenderSnapshot.dispose` | removed: call destroy() |

#### Classes that wait on a worker destroy asynchronously

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `OpfsClipPageProviderOptions.terminateWorkerOnClose` | `OpfsClipPageProviderOptions.terminateWorkerOnDestroy` |
| `OpfsClipStreamOptions.terminateWorkerOnClose` (`./worklet`) | `OpfsClipStreamOptions.terminateWorkerOnDestroy` |
| `OpfsClipStreamOptions.terminateWorkerOnClose` | `OpfsClipStreamOptions.terminateWorkerOnDestroy` |
| `VocalEditWorkerClient.dispose` | `VocalEditWorkerClient.destroy` |
| `VocalEditWorkerClientOptions.terminateWorkerOnDispose` | `VocalEditWorkerClientOptions.terminateWorkerOnDestroy` |
| `VocalEditWorkerSession.dispose` | `VocalEditWorkerSession.destroy` |

#### Physical quantities carry their unit in the name

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `Project.setClipFade(fadeIn)` | removed: pass it as fadeInPpq and fadeInCurve in ProjectClipFadeInput |
| `Project.setClipFade(fadeOut)` | removed: pass it as fadeOutPpq and fadeOutCurve in ProjectClipFadeInput |
| `Project.setClipFade` | setClipFade takes one { fadeInPpq, fadeInCurve, fadeOutPpq, fadeOutCurve } object instead of two ProjectClipFade objects |
| `ProjectClipFade` | removed: Call setClipFade(clipId, { fadeInPpq, fadeInCurve, fadeOutPpq, fadeOutCurve }) with one flat ProjectClipFadeInput. |

#### A value that is not given is absent, never 0, -1 or ''

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `Project.moveClip` | the optional track is options.trackId; an absent trackId keeps the track and an explicit 0 is a RangeError; a NaN, infinite or out-of-range newStartPpq is refused with RangeError naming it (1.x passed it through) |
| `Project.setClipTakes` | the active take is options.activeTakeId; absent means the base source and an explicit 0 is a RangeError |
| `Project.setMarker(markerId)` | removed: pass it as id in ProjectMarkerInput |
| `Project.setMarker(name)` | removed: pass name as a field of ProjectMarkerInput |
| `Project.setMarker(ppq)` | removed: pass ppq as a field of ProjectMarkerInput |
| `Project.setMarker` | setMarker takes one ProjectMarkerInput; an absent id allocates and an explicit 0 is a RangeError |
| `ProjectBounceOptions.numChannels` | an omitted width follows the scene master's layout (2 with no master) instead of always 2; the result's channels.length is the width used |
| `ProjectBounceOptions.sampleRate` | removed: Omit it; a bounce always renders at the project sample rate and ProjectBounceResult.sampleRate reports it. |
| `ProjectMidiRouteConfig.filterChannel` | filterChannel is typed number, not number \| null; a null at runtime still reads as absent |
| `ProjectMidiRouteConfig.filterGroup` | filterGroup is typed number, not number \| null; a null at runtime still reads as absent |
| `ProjectMidiRouteConfig.remapChannel` | remapChannel is typed number, not number \| null; a null at runtime still reads as absent |
| `ProjectTempoSegment.startSample` | removed: Drop it; give the segment startPpq only, since sample positions are derived when the project is compiled. |
| `ProjectVocalEditApplyRequest.renderedStartSample` | removed: Omit it; the field was required to be 0, and the rendered range now always starts at sample 0. |
| `ProjectVocalEditApplyRequest.takeId` | absent selects the base source; an explicit 0 is a RangeError |
| `ProjectVocalEditApplyResult.takeId` | absent when the base source was edited (was 0) |
| `ProjectVocalEditDependency.takeId` | absent when the base source was edited (was 0) |
| `ProjectVocalRehydrateItem.takeId` | absent when the base source was edited (was 0) |
| `VocalApplyRequest.expectedGeneration` | now optional; omitted means the draft's current generation |

#### A number outside its domain is refused, never passed through

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `ClipPageProvider.supply` | a channel list that is not array-like is refused with TypeError naming channels instead of a channel-count RangeError |
| `Project.addMidiClip` | a NaN, infinite or out-of-range startPpq or lengthPpq is refused with RangeError naming it (1.x passed it through) |
| `Project.duplicateClip` | a NaN, infinite or out-of-range newStartPpq is refused with RangeError naming it (1.x passed it through) |
| `Project.removeAutomationLane` | a NaN, infinite or out-of-range targetParamId is refused with RangeError naming it (1.x passed it through) |
| `Project.snapToGrid` | a NaN, infinite or out-of-range ppq or strength is refused with RangeError naming it (1.x passed it through) |
| `Project.splitClip` | a NaN, infinite or out-of-range splitPpq is refused with RangeError naming it (1.x passed it through) |
| `Project.trimClip` | a NaN, infinite or out-of-range newStartPpq or newLengthPpq is refused with RangeError naming it (1.x passed it through) |

#### String values are lowerCamelCase tokens

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `ProjectAutomationCurve='s-curve'` | `ProjectAutomationCurve='sCurve'` |
| `ProjectAutomationCurve='scurve'` | removed: spell it 'sCurve', the AutomationCurve token; 'scurve' is refused |
| `ProjectAutomationTargetKind='track-fader-db'` | `ProjectAutomationTargetKind='trackFaderDb'` |
| `ProjectAutomationTargetKind='track-pan'` | `ProjectAutomationTargetKind='trackPan'` |
| `ProjectFadeCurve='equal-power'` | removed: Use 'equalPower'; fade curves are 'linear', 'equalPower', 'exponential' and 'logarithmic'. |
| `ProjectFadeCurve='equal_power'` | removed: Use 'equalPower'; fade curves are 'linear', 'equalPower', 'exponential' and 'logarithmic'. |
| `ProjectFadeCurve='equalpower'` | removed: Use 'equalPower'; fade curves are 'linear', 'equalPower', 'exponential' and 'logarithmic'. |
| `ProjectFadeCurve='exp'` | removed: Use 'exponential'; fade curves are 'linear', 'equalPower', 'exponential' and 'logarithmic'. |
| `ProjectFadeCurve='log'` | removed: Use 'logarithmic'; fade curves are 'linear', 'equalPower', 'exponential' and 'logarithmic'. |

#### Closed sets are string unions, not numbers or IntEnums

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `AutomationTargetKind` | removed: Use ProjectAutomationTargetKind: the strings 'opaque', 'trackFaderDb' or 'trackPan' for targetKind. |
| `BuiltinSynthConfig.waveform` | the waveform is a name; a number is refused with TypeError |
| `PROJECT_AUTOMATION_TARGET_OPAQUE` | removed: Pass the string 'opaque' as targetKind; numeric target kinds are refused. |
| `PROJECT_AUTOMATION_TARGET_TRACK_FADER_DB` | removed: Pass the string 'trackFaderDb' as targetKind; numeric target kinds are refused. |
| `PROJECT_AUTOMATION_TARGET_TRACK_PAN` | removed: Pass the string 'trackPan' as targetKind; numeric target kinds are refused. |
| `Project.addAutomationLane` | targetKind is 'opaque' \| 'trackFaderDb' \| 'trackPan' |
| `Project.addTrack` | ProjectTrackDesc.kind is 'audio' \| 'midi' \| 'aux'; an ordinal is a TypeError |
| `Project.editAutomationLane` | targetKind is 'opaque' \| 'trackFaderDb' \| 'trackPan'; a NaN, infinite or out-of-range targetParamId is refused with RangeError naming it (1.x passed it through) |
| `Project.setClipWarpMode` | setClipWarpMode takes 'off' \| 'repitch' \| 'tempoSync' \| 'timeStretch'; an ordinal is a TypeError |
| `Project.setOverlapPolicy` | setOverlapPolicy takes 'disallow' \| 'allow'; an ordinal is a TypeError |
| `Project.setTrackKind` | setTrackKind takes 'audio' \| 'midi' \| 'aux'; an ordinal is a TypeError |
| `ProjectAutomationCurve` | the same tokens as AutomationCurve; an ordinal is a TypeError and the 'scurve' spelling is refused |
| `ProjectChordSymbol.quality` | a ProjectChordQuality token instead of an ordinal; a number is refused with TypeError |
| `ProjectKeySegment.mode` | a ProjectKeyMode token instead of an ordinal; a number is refused with TypeError |
| `ProjectMidiCcBinding.kind` | 'controlChange7' \| 'controlChange14' \| 'rpn' \| 'nrpn' (was 0 \| 1 \| 2 \| 3); an ordinal is a TypeError |
| `ProjectVocalEditDependency.reason` | VocalReason token instead of a number |
| `ProjectVocalReason` | `VocalReason` |
| `ProjectVocalRehydrateItem.reason` | VocalReason token instead of a number |
| `ProjectVocalRehydrateItem.status` | 'rehydrated' \| 'alreadyReady' \| 'unresolved' instead of 0 \| 1 \| 2 |
| `chordSymbolFromAnalysis` | quality is a ProjectChordQuality token ('major', 'halfDiminished', ...) instead of an ordinal |
| `keyModeFromAnalysis` | returns a ProjectKeyMode token ('major', 'dorian', ...) instead of an ordinal |

#### Results are typed values, not JSON strings

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|

| `ProjectCompileResult.diagnosticCount` | removed: Read diagnostics.length. |
| `ProjectCompileResult.hasTimeline` | removed: Check whether diagnostics holds an entry with severity 'error'; none means it compiled. compile({ withTimeline: true }) returns the timeline itself. |
| `ProjectCompileResult.messages` | removed: Read diagnostics, an array of ProjectDiagnostic, and use each entry's message. |
| `ProjectCompileTimelineResult` | removed: Use ProjectCompileResult; compile({ withTimeline: true }) fills its timeline. |

#### Cancellation uses signal for promises and cancel for sync calls

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `VocalEditWorkerTask` | removed: Await the promise VocalEditWorkerClient methods return; pass { signal } with an AbortController to cancel, which rejects with a SonareError coded Cancelled. |
| `VocalRenderRequest.signal` | `VocalRenderAsyncRequest.signal` |
| `VocalRenderRequest` | carries cancel?: () => boolean instead of signal and is the request of render only; renderAsync and the worker preview take VocalRenderAsyncRequest (range, requestId, signal) and beginRenderJob takes VocalRenderJobRequest (range, requestId) |
| `VocalRenderSnapshot.beginRenderJob` | takes VocalRenderJobRequest (range, requestId) and no signal; the caller stops the job with abort() |
| `VocalRenderSnapshot.renderAsync` | an already-aborted signal rejects with a Cancelled SonareError instead of a DOMException AbortError |
| `VocalRenderSnapshot.render` | takes cancel: () => boolean, polled between render work units, instead of signal; returning true throws a Cancelled SonareError with no partial PCM |

#### Synchronous construction is new X(config); create() is async

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `ClipPageProvider.constructor(engine)` | removed: pass { numChannels, numSamples, pageFrames }; the provider is no longer bound to an engine or addressed by id |
| `ClipPageProvider.constructor(id)` | removed: pass { numChannels, numSamples, pageFrames }; the provider is no longer bound to an engine or addressed by id |
| `ClipPageProvider.id` | removed: a clip names its provider by instance, not by id |
| `ClipPageProvider` | constructor(options: ClipPageProviderOptions) with { numChannels, numSamples, pageFrames } replaces construction through the engine; clear() after destroy() is InvalidState instead of a no-op |
| `ClipPageStreamer.constructor(engine)` | removed: pass the engine in the one options object: new ClipPageStreamer({ engine, readAheadPages, retainBehindPages, maxRequestsPerPump }) |
| `Project.create` | removed: call new Project() |
| `ProjectTimeline.constructor` | removed: not constructible; get a timeline from Project.compile({ withTimeline: true }) and install it with RealtimeEngine.applyProjectTimeline() |
| `VocalEditDraft.constructor` | removed: the constructor is protected; open a draft with VocalEditSession.beginEdit |
| `VocalEditSession.constructor` | removed: the constructor is protected; open a session with createVocalEditSession or restoreVocalEditSession |
| `VocalEditWorkerSession.constructor` | removed: the constructor is protected; open a session with VocalEditWorkerClient.create or VocalEditWorkerClient.restore |
| `VocalRenderJob.constructor` | removed: the constructor is protected; start a job with VocalRenderSnapshot.beginRenderJob |
| `VocalRenderSnapshot.constructor` | removed: the constructor is protected; take a snapshot with captureRenderSnapshot on a VocalEditSession or VocalEditDraft |
| `createOpfsClipPageProvider(engine)` | removed: createOpfsClipPageProvider(options) takes no engine; the clip names the provider instance |

| `VocalEditWorkerNativeDraft.commit(expectedRevision)` (`./vocal-edit-worker`) | `VocalEditWorkerNativeDraft.commit(options)`: receives { expectedRevision } instead of the revision string, the shape the session methods take |
| `VocalEditWorkerNativeDraft.exportState` (`./vocal-edit-worker`) | removed: Call exportState() on the session after the draft is committed; a draft no longer exports state. |
| `VocalEditWorkerNativeSession.beginEdit(expectedRevision)` (`./vocal-edit-worker`) | `VocalEditWorkerNativeSession.beginEdit(options)`: receives { expectedRevision } instead of the revision string, the shape the session methods take |
| `VocalEditWorkerNativeSession.redo(expectedRevision)` (`./vocal-edit-worker`) | `VocalEditWorkerNativeSession.redo(options)`: receives { expectedRevision } instead of the revision string, the shape the session methods take |
| `VocalEditWorkerNativeSession.undo(expectedRevision)` (`./vocal-edit-worker`) | `VocalEditWorkerNativeSession.undo(options)`: receives { expectedRevision } instead of the revision string, the shape the session methods take |
| `VocalEditWorkerSession.apply` | `VocalEditWorkerDraft.apply` |
| `VocalEditWorkerSession.beginEdit(options)` | pass { expectedRevision } instead of a bare revision string; a string is a TypeError naming the options shape |
| `VocalEditWorkerSession.beginEdit` | resolves to a VocalEditWorkerDraft instead of a state token |
| `VocalEditWorkerSession.cancel` | `VocalEditWorkerDraft.cancel` |
| `VocalEditWorkerSession.commit` | `VocalEditWorkerDraft.commit` |
| `VocalEditWorkerSession.redo(options)` | pass { expectedRevision } instead of a bare revision string; a string is a TypeError naming the options shape |
| `VocalEditWorkerSession.undo(options)` | pass { expectedRevision } instead of a bare revision string; a string is a TypeError naming the options shape |

#### Other individual changes

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `AlignTakeToReferenceRequest.binsPerOctave` | a value whose top chroma bin reaches half of sampleRate is a RangeError naming binsPerOctave and sampleRate (24 bins per octave needs a rate above 8 kHz); lower binsPerOctave or raise the rate (was a bare 'Invalid parameter') |
| `AlignTakeToReferenceRequest.hopLength` | an integer in [0, 65536] (RangeError 'alignTakeToReference: hopLength must be an integer in [0, 65536]'); 0 still selects the library hop; a negative hop was refused as a bare 'Invalid parameter' and a hop above 65536 was passed on to the constant-Q stage |
| `ClipPageStreamer.addSource` | pageFrames and numSamples are each refused by name unless an integer in [1, 9007199254740991]; a fractional size used to pass |
| `ClipPageStreamerRequest.clipId` | ClipPageStreamerRequest is the union ClipPageSampleRequest \| ClipPagePageRequest; clipId is on both members |
| `ClipPageStreamerRequest.pageIndex` | only on ClipPagePageRequest; narrow with "pageIndex" in request |
| `ClipPageStreamerRequest.sample` | only on ClipPageSampleRequest, which also carries channel; narrow with "sample" in request |
| `Project.setMixerSceneJson` | returns void (was one warning string per unknown key); an unknown scene key is refused as InvalidFormat naming the key, and a scene document is version 2: any other version is refused as InvalidFormat and an absent version reads as 2, so a stored 1.x scene needs version set to 2 and its surroundPan distance and elevation keys removed |
| `ProjectMidiCcBinding.ccLsbNumber` | an integer in [0, 127]; a value from 128 to 255 is a RangeError reading 'ccLsbNumber must be an integer in [0, 127]' under bindMidiCc, midiCcToBreakpoint and midiParamToCc (1.x let a selector byte in that range through and refused a bad controller number without naming the field) |
| `ProjectMidiCcBinding.ccNumber` | an integer in [0, 127]; a value from 128 to 255 is a RangeError reading 'ccNumber must be an integer in [0, 127]' under bindMidiCc, midiCcToBreakpoint and midiParamToCc (1.x let a selector byte in that range through and refused a bad controller number without naming the field) |
| `ProjectMidiCcBinding.selectorLsb` | an integer in [0, 127]; a value from 128 to 255 is a RangeError reading 'selectorLsb must be an integer in [0, 127]' under bindMidiCc, midiCcToBreakpoint and midiParamToCc (1.x let a selector byte in that range through and refused a bad controller number without naming the field) |
| `ProjectMidiCcBinding.selectorMsb` | an integer in [0, 127]; a value from 128 to 255 is a RangeError reading 'selectorMsb must be an integer in [0, 127]' under bindMidiCc, midiCcToBreakpoint and midiParamToCc (1.x let a selector byte in that range through and refused a bad controller number without naming the field) |
| `compareUint64` | removed: never callable: 1.x re-exported it type-only; a VocalUint64 is a decimal string, so order two values with BigInt(a) < BigInt(b) |
| `createSonareClipPageRequestRingBuffer` (`./worklet`) | `createClipPageRequestRingBuffer`: takes one options object { capacity } instead of positional numbers; an unknown key is a TypeError, a non-integer or out-of-domain value a RangeError |
| `sonareClipPageRequestRingBufferByteLength` (`./worklet`) | `clipPageRequestRingBufferByteLength`: takes one options object { capacity } instead of positional numbers; an unknown key is a TypeError, a non-integer or out-of-domain value a RangeError |
| `stateTokenEquals` | removed: never callable: 1.x re-exported it type-only; compare the VocalStateToken fields with ===, leaving out requestId (sessionEpoch, revision, draftId, generation, profileId) |
| `tokenEquals` | removed: never callable: 1.x re-exported it type-only; compare two VocalStateToken objects field by field with === (sessionEpoch, revision, draftId, generation, requestId, profileId) |

## Command line

The native `sonare-cli` and the Python `sonare` take the same commands, options and defaults; a row marked for one CLI applies to that front-end only. Input files are positional arguments. A failure exits with the code of its cause on both front-ends: 2 a usage error (decided before the input is read), 3 an invalid parameter, 4 an input that cannot be found or read, 5 a document that cannot be parsed, 6 audio that cannot be decoded, 7 out of memory, 8 not supported, 9 invalid state, 10 another error, 11 cancelled, 12 an output that cannot be written, 13 an ABI mismatch (Python only) and 14 a stale result. `SONARE_LEGACY_EXIT` is not read.

### Command line: Loading, versions, audio buffers and errors

#### Sample rate is spelled sampleRate, sample_rate and --sample-rate

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `chirp --sr` (native CLI only) | `chirp --sample-rate`: renamed --sample-rate; a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `clicks --sr` (native CLI only) | `clicks --sample-rate`: renamed --sample-rate; a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `clicks` (native CLI only) | the JSON sr key is sample_rate, named as the flag is |
| `tone --sr` (native CLI only) | `tone --sample-rate`: renamed --sample-rate; a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |

#### Seconds are spelled Sec and _sec

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `chirp --duration` (native CLI only) | `chirp --duration-sec` |
| `clicks --click-duration` (native CLI only) | `clicks --click-duration-sec` |
| `tone --duration` (native CLI only) | `tone --duration-sec` |

#### Physical quantities carry their unit in the name

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `clicks --frequency` (native CLI only) | `clicks --frequency-hz` |
| `tone --frequency` (native CLI only) | `tone --frequency-hz` |
| `tone` (native CLI only) | the JSON frequency key is frequency_hz and sr is sample_rate, named as the flags are; leaving out --frequency-hz is refused as a usage error (exit 2) rather than exit 3 |

#### A value that is not given is absent, never 0, -1 or ''

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `clicks --length` (native CLI only) | leaving it out ends the track after the last click and its decay; the option no longer states a 0 default, and a spelled value outside 1 to 500000000 (the library's offline length cap) is refused as a usage error (exit 2) rather than read as the same thing as leaving it out |
| `fix-frames --x-max` (native CLI only) | leaving it out means no upper bound; the option no longer states a -1 default, and a spelled negative value is refused as a usage error (exit 2) rather than read as the same thing as leaving it out |

#### An option left out takes the library's default

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `frame-signal --n-fft` (native CLI only) | removed: give the frame length as --frame-length |
| `frame-signal` (native CLI only) | --frame-length and --hop-length are required, as the library takes no default for either; give --frame-length 2048 --hop-length 512 to keep the 1.x framing |
| `frames-to-samples --frames` (native CLI only) | leaving it out is refused as a usage error (exit 2) rather than converting frame 0 |
| `frames-to-samples --n-fft` (native CLI only) | omitted, no centring offset is applied, as the library does; pass --n-fft 2048 to keep the 1.x offset of 1024 samples; a spelled value below 1 is refused as a usage error (exit 2) rather than read as the same thing as omitting it |
| `peak-pick` (native CLI only) | --pre-max, --post-max, --pre-avg, --post-avg, --delta and --wait are required, as the library takes no default for any of them; give --pre-max 1 --post-max 1 --pre-avg 1 --post-avg 1 --delta 0 --wait 0 to keep the 1.x result |
| `samples-to-frames --n-fft` (native CLI only) | omitted, no centring offset is applied, as the library does; pass --n-fft 2048 to keep the 1.x offset of 1024 samples; a spelled value below 1 is refused as a usage error (exit 2) rather than read as the same thing as omitting it |
| `samples-to-frames --samples` (native CLI only) | leaving it out is refused as a usage error (exit 2) rather than converting sample 0 |

#### Frequency bounds are f0MinHz/f0MaxHz and fminHz/fmaxHz

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `chirp --fmax` (native CLI only) | `chirp --fmax-hz`: renamed --fmax-hz and required; leaving it out, or giving 0 or a negative value, is a usage error (exit 2) |
| `chirp --fmin` (native CLI only) | `chirp --fmin-hz`: renamed --fmin-hz; a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `chirp` (native CLI only) | the JSON fmin and fmax keys are fmin_hz and fmax_hz and sr is sample_rate, named as the flags are |

### Command line: Analysis and features

#### Seconds are spelled Sec and _sec

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `chords --min-duration` | `chords --min-duration-sec` |
| `sections --min-duration` | `sections --min-duration-sec`: renamed --min-duration-sec; a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |

#### Physical quantities carry their unit in the name

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `analyze` | the --json result names the loudness range loudness_range_lu rather than loudness_range_db |
| `clipping --threshold` (native CLI only) | `clipping --threshold-db`: the detection level is given in dBFS as --threshold-db, in [-120, 0]; a linear threshold t becomes 20*log10(t), and a level outside the range is refused as a usage error (exit 2) |
| `dynamics` | the --json result names the loudness range loudness_range_lu rather than loudness_range_db |
| `meter --clip-threshold` (native CLI only) | `meter --clip-threshold-db`: the clipping level is given in dBFS as --clip-threshold-db, in [-120, 0]; a linear threshold t becomes 20*log10(t), and a level outside the range is refused as a usage error (exit 2) |

#### A value that is not given is absent, never 0, -1 or ''

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `acoustic` | the JSON no longer carries is_blind: a blind estimate omits edt, c50, c80, d50 and their band arrays, so test for edt instead |
| `estimate-room --n-octave-bands` | omitted, the library chooses the band count; an explicit 0 or a negative value is refused as a usage error (exit 2) rather than read as the default, and the refusal states the upper bound the field holds ("must be an integer in [N, 2147483647]") |
| `melody` (native CLI only) | the JSON drops has_melody, mean_frequency becomes mean_frequency_hz and vibrato_rate becomes vibrato_rate_hz; with no voiced frame pitch_range_octaves, mean_frequency_hz, pitch_stability and vibrato_rate_hz are absent rather than 0, so test for mean_frequency_hz |
| `vocal-notes` | the JSON note record no longer carries has_pitch: the pitch keys (median_hz, center_midi, f0_stability, note_name, cents) are absent on an unpitched note, so test for center_midi instead |

#### An option left out takes the library's default

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `analyze --meter-candidates` | omitted, the core's candidate set (3,4,6) applies; an explicit empty value and an entry that is not an integer are refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read rather than read as not given |
| `key --modes` | omitted, the library's candidate modes apply; an explicit empty value and an unknown mode are refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read rather than read as not given, and entries are no longer trimmed of spaces on the Python front-end |
| `key --profile` | omitted, the genre hint chooses the profile; an explicit empty value and an unknown profile name are refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read rather than read as not given |
| `melody --fmax` (native CLI only) | `melody --f0-max-hz`: renamed --f0-max-hz; omitted, the library default (2093 Hz) applies rather than 1000 Hz; pass the 1.x value to keep 1.x output; a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `melody --fmin` (native CLI only) | `melody --f0-min-hz`: renamed --f0-min-hz; omitted, the library default (65 Hz) applies rather than 80 Hz; pass the 1.x value to keep 1.x output; a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `melody --hop-length` (native CLI only) | omitted, the library hop of 256 samples applies rather than 512; pass --hop-length 512 to keep 1.x output; a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3), and the refusal states the upper bound the field holds ("must be an integer in [N, 2147483647]") |
| `mfcc-to-audio --n-mfcc` (native CLI only) | omitted, 20 coefficients are kept, the library's MFCC default, rather than 13; pass --n-mfcc 13 to keep the 1.x result |
| `vqt --gamma` (native CLI only) | omitted, the library derives the bandwidth offset from the ERB bandwidths rather than using 0 (a constant-Q transform); pass --gamma 0 to keep 1.x output; a negative value is refused as a usage error (exit 2) rather than read as the derived offset |

### Command line: Effects, separation, repair and room acoustics

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `resample --target-rate` | `resample --target-sample-rate` |

#### An option left out takes the library's default

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `pitch-correct --current-midi` | required: an omitted --current-midi no longer reads as MIDI 69 (A4) and is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, as the library assumes no pitch; pass 69 to keep the 1.x result |
| `pitch-correct --target-midi` | required: an omitted --target-midi no longer reads as MIDI 69 (A4) and is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, as the library assumes no pitch; pass 69 to keep the 1.x result |

#### String values are lowerCamelCase tokens

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `filter --type` (native CLI only) | is required and takes the library's response names in kebab-case (high-pass, low-pass, band-pass, notch); hp, lp, bp, highpass, lowpass, bandpass and any other spelling or letter case are refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read |
| `voice-change --preset` | a built-in preset is named by its library id (neutralMonitor, brightIdol, hardTune, ...) in any letter case, and the JSON preset field reports that id; the kebab-case spellings, an unknown id, an empty value, a selector combination and a malformed --set assignment are refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, with one text on both front-ends, the empty value no longer read as not given; a --preset-pack entry is matched by its id exactly as written |
| `voice-preset --preset` | takes the library preset id in any letter case and defaults to neutralMonitor; the kebab-case spellings and an unknown id are refused as a usage error (exit 2) naming the accepted ids |
| `voice-presets` | lists the library preset ids (neutralMonitor, brightIdol, ...) rather than their kebab-case spellings |

#### Errors are coded by cause on every surface

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `voice-change --preset-json` | a preset document the library refuses (an unknown field, an earlier schemaVersion) exits 5 as an invalid format on the native CLI too, rather than 3 |

| `pitch-shift` | the JSON semitones key is pitch_semitones, named as the flag is |

### Command line: Mastering, mixing and loudness

#### Physical quantities carry their unit in the name

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `lufs` | the --json result names the loudness range loudness_range_lu rather than loudness_range |

#### Loudness quantities use one name per measurement

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `mastering --ceiling-db` | `mastering --ceiling-dbtp` |
| `mastering-streaming --platforms` | each platform is exactly {name, target_lufs, ceiling_dbtp}, all three required; targetLufs, ceilingDb, ceilingDbtp and ceiling_db are refused as unknown keys with the accepted list, and a missing target or ceiling no longer defaults to -14 LUFS / -1 dB; a document refused on any of these grounds, or as not an array of platform objects, an empty or non-string name or a non-number target, is a usage error (exit 2) reported as "argument --platforms: <reason>" before the input is read, while a --platforms-file document is still refused after it (exit 3) |
| `mastering-suggest --ceiling-db` | `mastering-suggest --ceiling-dbtp` |

#### A value that is not given is absent, never 0, -1 or ''

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `suggest-mix --tempo-bpm` | the flag takes auto or a tempo greater than 0; an explicit 0, a negative or a non-number is refused as a usage error naming the flag, and leaving it out (no longer an empty string) keeps the transport's fallback tempo |

#### String values are lowerCamelCase tokens

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `mix-strip --pan-mode` | takes balance, stereo-pan or dual-pan in any letter case; stereopan, dualpan and the scene JSON's stereoPan / dualPan are refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read |

#### Python keyword arguments and attributes are snake_case only

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `suggest-mix` | the JSON keys tracks, mix and the keys beside scene in snake_case (strip_id, num_channels, integrated_lufs, band_dominance, track_count ...), as mastering-suggest does; scene keeps the scene schema's names because mix --scene reads it back, band tokens keying band_occupancy stay tokens, and a track's name, exclusion_reason or integrated_lufs is absent rather than null when not measured |

#### Errors are coded by cause on every surface

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `mastering --chain-config` | the Python CLI reads the document through the library's chain-config reader, as the native CLI does: a document it refuses (an unknown or earlier key, a value outside its domain, a version 2 document without a complete multiband block) exits 5 as an invalid format rather than 3, and the chain runs with every parameter the document leaves out at its default |

#### masterAudio is the mastering entry; mastering is renamed

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `mastering --true-peak-oversample` | removed: use mastering-normalize-loudness --true-peak-oversample, or --params loudness.truePeakOversample=N on a mastering chain |
| `mastering` | a chain is required: --preset or --chain-config, or --assistant (which may take --preset as its base); with none the command is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, instead of normalising loudness, which is now mastering-normalize-loudness with the same options and output; --chain-config alongside --preset or --assistant is refused the same way; --target-lufs, --ceiling-dbtp, --enable-repair, --explain, --target-platform, --no-streaming-safe and --speech-mono-amount reach only the assistant and are refused without --assistant (exit 2, before the input is read); the JSON mode for a chain read from --chain-config is chainConfig rather than config, naming the option that chose the chain; the before and after summaries of --report name the loudness range loudness_range_lu rather than loudness_range |

#### Stereo-only algorithms take left and right

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `repair` | a stereo input is measured per channel and repaired as a stereo pair, writing a stereo file; it was downmixed to mono; --detect alongside --explain, --preset, --stages, --params or --bits, --stages alongside --preset, --explain alongside --stages or --preset, an unknown or repeated --stages name and a --params key outside repair.* are refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) after it; --explain beside --detect, --preset or --stages is refused on both CLIs as "--explain cannot be combined with <option>" |

#### Historical aliases are removed

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `eq --lookahead-ms` | removed: use --detector-delay-ms |
| `mastering --config` | removed: use --chain-config |

#### Both CLIs share command names, flags, defaults and failures

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `eq --bits` | a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `eq --coeff-mode` | a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `eq --phase-mode` | a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `eq --placement` | a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `eq --resolution` | a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `eq --type` | a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `master` (python CLI only) | removed: use mastering with --preset (master's default was pop), --chain-config or --assistant; each --config leaf goes to --params as path=value |
| `mastering --bits` | a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `mastering --params` | an entry that is not key=value is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, with the one text 'argument --params: must be a comma-separated list of key=value entries' on both front-ends and on repair, eq, mastering-processor, mastering-pair-processor, mastering-pair-analyze, mastering-stereo-analyze, mastering-profile and mastering-suggest; the text no longer echoes the entry |
| `mastering --preset` | a name outside the catalog is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read with 'argument --preset: must be one of ...'; the same holds for repair --preset, mastering-suggest --preset, mastering-processor --processor, mastering-pair-processor --processor, mastering-pair-analyze --analysis and mastering-stereo-analyze --analysis |
| `mastering-chain` (python CLI only) | removed: use mastering --chain-config with a version-2 document, {"version":2,"params":<the old config>} |
| `mastering-pair-processor --bits` | a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `mastering-processor --bits` | a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `mastering-processor --params` | a key the processor does not read is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, as is a shortcut option beside eq --params (the first one supplied is named) and an earlier mastering-suggest --params spelling or a setting given both as an option and as a key |
| `mix-strip --pan` | a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `mix-strip --width` | a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `repair --bits` | a value outside the accepted set is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `repair --output` | leaving it out without --detect, or giving it with --detect, is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `suggest-mix --input` | an entry with an empty track id or an empty path, and a call with no entry, are refused as a usage error (exit 2) before any input is read |
| `suggest-mix --params` | a malformed entry, a non-numeric value, an unknown or snake_case key and a tempoBpm clash with --tempo-bpm are refused as a usage error (exit 2) before any input is read, with one text on both front-ends |

### Command line: Realtime engine, synthesis, MIDI and playback

#### String values are lowerCamelCase tokens

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `playback --room` | values are kebab-case (living-room, home-theater, screening-room), read in any letter case; the snake_case spellings are refused as a usage error (exit 2) |
| `project.bounce --synth` | takes the library synth preset id (sawLead, warmPad, ...) in any letter case; the kebab-case spellings and a name no NativeSynth preset carries are refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the project is read |
| `project.synth-presets` | lists the library synth preset ids (sawLead, warmPad, ...) rather than their kebab-case spellings |

#### Both CLIs share command names, flags, defaults and failures

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `mix --input` (python CLI only) | an entry with an empty strip id or an empty path is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before any input is read |
| `mix --output` (python CLI only) | giving it without --input, or --input without it, is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |
| `mix --sample-rate` (python CLI only) | a rate outside 8000-384000 is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before any input is read |
| `playback --output` | leaving it out is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3) |

#### Other individual changes

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `mix --block-size` (python CLI only) | removed, no replacement: the rendered mix does not depend on the block size the mixer is driven with; leave the flag out |

### Command line: Projects, arrangement and vocal editing

#### Physical quantities carry their unit in the name

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `midi-render --instrument-latency` | `midi-render --instrument-latency-samples` |
| `project.bounce --instrument-latency` | `project.bounce --instrument-latency-samples` |

#### A value that is not given is absent, never 0, -1 or ''

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `midi-render --channels` | omitted, the render takes the scene master's layout width rather than 2; an explicit 0 or a negative value is refused as a usage error (exit 2) rather than read as the default; a width no speaker layout has (not 1, 2, 6 or 8) is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3), and the refusal states the upper bound the field holds ("must be an integer in [N, 2147483647]") |
| `midi-render --frames` | omitted, the length is derived from the project (no longer 0 spelled by the CLI); an explicit 0 or a negative value is refused as a usage error (exit 2), and the count is read at 64 bits, so a value past 2147483647 is accepted |
| `project.bounce --channels` | omitted, the render takes the scene master's layout width rather than 2; an explicit 0 or a negative value is refused as a usage error (exit 2) rather than read as the default; a width no speaker layout has (not 1, 2, 6 or 8) is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read, rather than as an invalid parameter (exit 3), and the refusal states the upper bound the field holds ("must be an integer in [N, 2147483647]") |
| `project.bounce --frames` | omitted, the length is derived from the project (no longer 0 spelled by the CLI); an explicit 0 or a negative value is refused as a usage error (exit 2), and the count is read at 64 bits, so a value past 2147483647 is accepted |

#### An option left out takes the library's default

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `midi-render --synth` | omitted, notes follow GM program and channel routing; an explicit empty value and a name no NativeSynth preset carries are refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the project is read, the empty value no longer read as GM routing |
| `project.align-takes --bins-per-octave` | omitted, the library's chroma resolution applies; an explicit 0 is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read rather than read as the library value, and the refusal states the upper bound the field holds ("must be an integer in [N, 2147483647]") |
| `project.align-takes --hop-length` | omitted, the library's chroma hop applies; an explicit 0 is refused as a usage error (exit 2) before the input is read rather than read as the library value, and the refusal states the upper bound the field holds ("must be an integer in [N, 2147483647]") |
| `project.new --sample-rate` | omitted, the project keeps its own rate; an explicit 0 or any rate outside 8000-384000 is refused as a usage error (exit 2) rather than read as not given |

#### CLI input is a positional argument

| 1.x | 2.0.0 |
